papers.title: Elevated-temperature wear behaviour of LPBF Ti-6Al-4V for aero-engine turbine applications
papers.abstract: The elevated-temperature wear properties of Ti-6Al-4V alloy synthesised by laser powder bed fusion is thoroughly examined in this work, with an emphasis on its suitability for use in aero-engine turbine conditions. Using a pin-on-disc tribometer, systematic dry sliding wear studies were executed throughout a temperature range from 150°C to 350°C by adjusting important factors such as sliding speed, normal load, and sliding time. With values ranging from 0.0076 g at 150°C to 0.0220 g at 350°C, the results demonstrate that wear loss raises dramatically with temperature and normal load, clearly showing a shift from mild to severe wear regimes. Temperature-dependent oxidation behaviour was shown by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), where material degradation is accelerated at elevated temperatures because of the instability of protective oxide layers, which limit wear at intermediate temperatures. The development of wear processes from mild adhesive and abrasive wear at lower temperatures to severe oxidative, delamination, and three-body abrasive wear at higher temperatures was verified by FESEM analysis. The results provide a basis for developing LPBF Ti-6Al-4V components for high-temperature aerospace applications and emphasise the crucial role that oxidation and load play in controlling wear performance.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了LPBF Ti-6Al-4V的高温磨损行为，但未涉及拉伸或疲劳等核心力学性能。
llm.why_not_core: Does not report tensile, yield, fatigue, or other bulk mechanical properties listed in the focus; instead focuses on wear, which is a surface degradation property rather than the core mechanical/fatigue characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估LPBF Ti-6Al-4V在航空发动机涡轮工况下的高温磨损性能。
summary_zh.method: 采用销盘式摩擦磨损试验机，在150-350°C下进行干滑动磨损实验，结合TGA和FESEM分析。
summary_zh.result: 磨损量随温度和载荷增加而显著增大，从轻微磨损转变为严重磨损，归因于氧化层失稳。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验测试和微观表征验证磨损机制和氧化行为。

summary_en.motivation: This work investigates the elevated-temperature wear behavior of LPBF Ti-6Al-4V alloy for potential application in aero-engine turbine environments.
summary_en.method: Dry sliding wear tests were conducted using a pin-on-disc tribometer over a temperature range of 150-350°C with varying sliding speed, normal load, and time, complemented by thermogravimetric analysis and FESEM.
summary_en.result: Wear loss increased significantly with temperature and load, transitioning from mild adhesive and abrasive wear to severe oxidative, delamination, and three-body abrasive wear due to oxide layer instability.
summary_en.validation: The wear mechanisms and oxidation behavior were validated through controlled experiments and microstructural characterization.

papers.title: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence in Metallic Orthopedic Implant Development: A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Background: Metallic orthopedic implants face persistent clinical challenges that have proved resistant to incremental conventional development. Machine learning and artificial intelligence offer a complementary paradigm for navigating the high-dimensional design spaces governing implant performance, yet the literature remains fragmented across disciplinary silos with no comprehensive synthesis spanning the full development pipeline. Methods: A structured database search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane (executed May 2026), supplemented by hand-searching of reference lists, identified 33 primary studies organized across five sequential domains: alloy composition discovery, additive manufacturing process–property optimization, lattice and porous structure design, surface engineering and coatings, and corrosion and wear prediction. Results: Across all five domains, machine learning approaches, including random forests, convolutional neural networks, Bayesian optimization, generative adversarial networks, physics-informed neural networks, and autonomous multi-agent platforms, have accelerated property prediction and design space exploration beyond experimental or simulation-based methods. Shared barriers to translation include small, heterogeneous datasets, reliance on internal rather than external validation, limited interpretability, and the absence of regulatory frameworks for AI-assisted device design. Representative performance included modulus predictions within ~4 GPa of first-principles values, ML-designed alloys reaching ~42.7 GPa (versus 103–120 GPa for Ti-6Al-4V), property prediction R2 often above 0.90 (up to 0.96–0.9991), 98.3% corrosion severity classification accuracy, and acceleration from a roughly fivefold reduction in finite element simulations to surrogates compressing days into minutes. Conclusions: Addressing these limitations will require open standardized databases linking materials parameters to registry-level clinical outcomes, prospective clinical validation studies, and coordinated engagement between researchers, industry, and regulatory agencies.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文为综述，涉及金属骨科植入物开发的机器学习方法，但未具体针对Ti-6Al-4V股骨柄的结构设计或力学性能。
llm.why_not_core: This is a narrative review covering ML/AI in metallic implant development broadly, not a primary study on Ti-6Al-4V femoral stem design, fatigue, or experimental validation.

summary_zh.motivation: 传统方法难以解决金属骨科植入物的临床挑战，需新范式加速开发。
summary_zh.method: 对五个领域（合金成分、增材制造、多孔结构、表面工程、腐蚀磨损）的33项研究进行综述。
summary_zh.result: 机器学习在性能预测和设计空间探索上显著加速，但面临数据小、缺乏外部验证等障碍。
summary_zh.validation: 无原始验证，基于文献汇总的模型性能指标。

summary_en.motivation: Clinical challenges in metallic orthopedic implants persist despite incremental conventional development, motivating the use of machine learning to navigate high-dimensional design spaces.
summary_en.method: A structured database search identified 33 primary studies across five domains: alloy discovery, AM process optimization, lattice design, surface engineering, and corrosion/wear prediction.
summary_en.result: ML approaches (random forests, CNNs, Bayesian optimization, GANs, PINNs) achieved property predictions within ~4 GPa of first-principles values and R² above 0.90, but translation barriers include small datasets and lack of external validation.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; reported performance metrics are compiled from reviewed studies.
